$comment: Agents (SPEC §12, #6): the opentide MCP server definition provider, the fork fallback, and two language-model tools for live editor state. No chatSkills: the opentidehq/skills Agent Plugin is recommended (wizard, walkthrough), not embedded, until the EUPL licence review in #6, and embedded skills would load twice beside the plugin. No chat participant.

languageModelTools.name: opentide_open_file_diagnostics
languageModelTools.userDescription: The problems VS Code shows for a file: the language server's, opentide validate's and lint's.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns every diagnostic VS Code currently shows for one file, merged across the opentide language server, `opentide validate` and `opentide lint` (and other extensions), with severity, source, code, message and 1-based line/column ranges. Use it for the live state of a file the user is editing, including unsaved changes the language server has checked. Defaults to the active editor's file. For workspace-wide validation, use the opentide MCP server's tools instead.

file.description: An absolute path, or a path relative to the first workspace folder. Omit for the active editor's file.

languageModelTools.name: opentide_active_object
languageModelTools.userDescription: The Tide object in the active editor, its UUID and what it connects to.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the opentide object (threat, objective or rule) open in the active editor: its UUID, type, schema, name, TLP, platforms, techniques and tactics, why its file did not load (load_error) when it did not, and its graph neighbourhood one hop away (the objects, signals, ATT&CK techniques and log sources it points to or that point to it, with the edge kind and field path). Use it to learn what the user is looking at. For the whole catalogue, search or validation, use the opentide MCP server's tools instead.

commands.title: Add opentide to This Editor's MCP Settings
Remove opentide from This Editor's MCP Settings

enumDescriptions: Provide the opentide MCP server to VS Code's agents, unless a workspace MCP file (`.vscode/mcp.json`, `.mcp.json`) already defines an `opentide` server VS Code can start. When that server's command is not found, the extension's is named `opentide (VS Code)`.
Always provide it; VS Code shows one `opentide` server when a workspace file defines one too, and names the extension's `opentide (VS Code)` when the file's command is not found.
opentide.mcp.provide.markdownDescription: Whether the extension gives VS Code's agents the opentide MCP server (`opentide mcp start` with the resolved runtime). Off in Restricted Mode, where this setting is not read.

enumDescriptions: Ask once before adding the opentide MCP server to the user-level MCP file of Kiro, Devin Desktop or Windsurf, which have no extension API for it.
Add it, and keep it current, without asking.
opentide.agents.writeEditorConfig.markdownDescription: Whether the extension writes an `opentide` entry into the user-level MCP file of an editor with no extension API for MCP servers (Kiro, Devin Desktop, Windsurf), and keeps it current when the extension updates. It only ever rewrites or removes an entry it wrote itself, marked `OPENTIDE_VSCODE_EXTENSION`. Cursor and VS Code get the server from the extension directly, and no file is written.

opentide.mcp.useBundled.markdownDescription: Run the MCP server with the opentide module the extension carries even where an opentide is installed. With no opentide installed the bundled module is used anyway. Tenant tools (deploy, live validate, query) work through the extension; see the bundled MCP server in the README.
